method: Offline only: committed corpus trips and place cache, deterministic probes (src/tripplanner/evals/probes.py), the existing trip audit, and itinerary-v1 judgements of 12 corpus trips. No trip was planned and no Google API was called.

findings.title: Activity labels, clock times and region phrases are sent to Google Places and the first result is accepted as the place
findings.prevalence: 451 of 3,975 cached resolutions (11.3%) share no word with the stop name
findings.evidence: "India Gate | delhi, agra, jaipur" -> tour agency "Delhi Agra Jaipur Trip" (42 stops resolve to it); "Meetings (User's location) | new york" -> New York Inter-Group of AA; "Harajuku" -> a gyukatsu restaurant; "Kamadgiri" -> Kashi Vishwanath (wrong city); "Ross Island" -> Aberdeen Jetty; 17 clock times ("08:00") and prompt sentences ("key details:") were paid lookups. Today's filters (places_cache.is_lookupable_place_name and place_confidence.stop_place_tier) both still pass "08:00", "Work meetings", "Lunch break" and "Sunset at beach". Hand review of a random 40 of the mismatches: about 30 were a wrong place or a non-place label.
findings.impact: Confident map pins in the wrong place (sometimes the wrong city), wrong photos and ratings in the stop card, and paid Places calls that buy nothing.
findings.fix: One stop classifier shared by lookup gating and map tiering that rejects times, activity phrases and sentences; bias each lookup with the stop's own city rather than the whole destination phrase; and accept a result only when its name shares a token with the query or its type matches the stop kind, otherwise store it as approximate and never pin it.
findings.source: LLM judge (New York, Tokyo, Cape Town packets) then deterministic place_identity probe
findings.resolution: places_cache now declines clock times, sentences and activity labels (via place_confidence, which learned the missing words), requests five candidates in the same single billed search and keeps the one named like the stop, and never shows or pins a cached result that shares no word with it. On the committed cache: 272 distinct non-place names would no longer be bought, and 322 wrong results are hidden. City bias still uses the caller's context. Tests: tests/test_places_cache.py.

findings.title: Provider test-mode offers are saved as real, priced flights
findings.prevalence: 9 of 178 corpus trips; 9 of the 13 trips that have any selected flight
findings.evidence: "Duffel Airways" (flight numbers ZZ…) in 6 trips, e.g. Cape Town $596.75, Bhutan $1,206.54; "Nuitée Air" from liteapi in 3 trips, e.g. Goa ₹29,582. tools/duffel_flights.py documents that duffel_test_ tokens return synthetic offers, but nothing marks them after selection.
findings.impact: A traveller or the booking handoff can present a fare that does not exist; budget totals include invented prices.
findings.fix: Mark every offer from a test-mode credential or known sandbox carrier as synthetic at the provider adapter; refuse to persist it in selected_flights or the booking handoff; if kept for development, label it "Sample fare, not bookable" in every view.
findings.source: LLM judge (Cape Town, Goa) then synthetic_fares probe

findings.title: Stops are listed after the journey that already left them
findings.prevalence: A stay listed after the day's departure in 95 of 178 trips (143 stays); out-of-order times in 26 trips (28 stops)
findings.evidence: Tokyo day 4: Shinkansen 09:00 then Sunroute checkout 12:10; Gujarat day 3: drive 08:00 then Ahmedabad checkout 14:30; Rajasthan day 3: Jaipur checkout 18:00 after reaching Jodhpur, "Lunch break" 20:00; Char Dham days 3-7 repeat the pattern; Andaman: Port Blair checkout after the Havelock ferry.
findings.impact: The itinerary, the map route and the day's travel totals describe an impossible order; audit rules I4/I9 fire on the symptom rather than the cause.
findings.fix: A deterministic normaliser on save: origin-hotel checkout precedes the first departing move, timed stops sort by time, and a stop whose time runs backwards is rejected back to the agent with the exact conflict instead of being saved.
findings.source: LLM judge (5 of 12 trips) then deterministic probes
findings.resolution: tools/day_order.py runs on every save: a stay that is being left (a check-out, a 'start from hotel', or the previous night's hotel before any return journey) moves to just before the day's first departure and loses an impossible time. Out-of-order times were already rejected by the chronology check merged on 2026-09-12; all 26 corpus cases predate it. On the corpus, simulated saves take misplaced stays from 95 trips to 0. Tests: tests/test_day_order.py.

findings.title: The selected hotel keeps a paid night after the traveller has flown or driven home
findings.evidence: Paris: Hotel Le Littre to 12 Apr, flight home 11 Apr; Tokyo: Granvia Kyoto to 9 Apr, flight 8 Apr; Mysore: Radisson to 15 Sep, drive home 14 Sep and a 'Buffer/Return' day 6 at the hotel; Bali-honeymoon: Mulia to 19 Nov, leaves 18 Nov. Contributing cause: every generated request phrases an N-day trip across N+1 calendar dates (matrix._compose uses start + days), and checkout copies return_date. The deterministic audit reports "Itinerary covers N of N+1 requested days" 241 times across the corpus.
findings.impact: Budget totals include a night nobody uses, and the plan invents filler days at a hotel after departure.
findings.fix: Checkout equals the date of the departing journey; when the request's day count and date span disagree, ask once instead of silently choosing; generate corpus requests with an end date of start + days - 1.
findings.source: LLM judge (Paris, Tokyo, Mysore) then unused_nights probe
findings.resolution: The same save-time step checks out on the day the trip ends with the journey home and re-prices the stay from its nightly rate (20 corpus trips to 0 when re-saved). The generation matrices now phrase an N-day trip as N calendar days; the manifest keeps the original requests of the 178 existing trips.

findings.title: Plans are completed with placeholder hotels, meals and journeys
findings.prevalence: The audit's own completion-gap gate fails on 329 of 349 trips (1,331 hits); 75 of 178 corpus trips hold 544 placeholder stops; 88 of 178 carry no priced item at all
findings.evidence: Goa ("We want … good food") has five TBD meals; Rajasthan's every meal is "Local restaurant <city>"; Char Dham and Kerala have only "Hotel in <city>"; New York has "Hotel (TBD)" on every day. prompts.py forbids leaving TBD meals, but trip_validation only warns and the plan still completes. Paris uses "Central Paris Hotel" instead of the selected Hotel Le Littre (10 of 102 trips with a selected hotel do not name it in the itinerary). Audit I6 finds 459 nights with no concrete, bookable stay.
findings.impact: The traveller receives an itinerary that reads as decided but is not; judged meal quality averages 2.58/5, second lowest after narrative coherence (2.50).
findings.fix: Count placeholders deterministically at the completion gate and either fill them from research already in hand or return them as explicit open decisions (UX Lab 32); bind hotel stops to selected_hotels by id rather than by name.
findings.source: LLM judge (all 12 trips) then placeholder_stops probe
findings.resolution: Not approved in this round; UX Lab 32 covers the presentation side.

findings.title: Explicit asks in the request are dropped without saying so
findings.evidence: Paris: "Include the flights" -> no selected flight; Bali: "Verify current official entry requirements" -> no visa or advisory section; Char Dham: 2 of 4 dhams with no explanation; Goa: "good food" -> all meals TBD.
findings.impact: The plan looks complete to the traveller while missing the one thing they asked for.
findings.fix: Extract explicit asks into a request checklist at kickoff and have the completion gate require each to be Met or Dropped with a stated reason.
findings.resolution: tools/request_asks.py reads the traveller's words from the turn that created the trip. 'Include the flights', 'verify entry requirements' and 'covering A, B and C' (with named circuits such as Char Dham) become first-turn completion gaps unless met or recorded in the new dropped_requests field with a reason the agent must also say. On the corpus it flags 18 trips: 16 missing entry checks, Paris flights and Char Dham. Tests: tests/test_request_asks.py.

findings.title: Day summaries promise stops that are on other days
findings.evidence: Lonavala day 2 summary: "Visit Bhushi Dam, Tiger Point"; those are on days 3 and 1. Dubai day 1 names Burj Khalifa (day 2); Amritsar day 2 names the Golden Temple (day 1).
findings.impact: The day card contradicts itself, so the traveller cannot trust either the summary or the stops.
findings.fix: Rebuild the summary line from the day's stops after every edit, or validate that every place it names is on that day.
findings.resolution: trip_validation.summary_drift_warnings is a first-turn completion gap: a summary naming another day's stop must be rewritten from that day's stops (10 corpus trips).

findings.title: Long drives are scheduled at impossible average speeds
findings.evidence: Rajasthan day 1: Mumbai to Jaipur 1,160 km in 660 minutes (105 km/h door to door), followed by an 18:00 bazaar stroll; Tirupati-Hyderabad 550 km in 7 hours.
findings.impact: A day that cannot be driven; the audit's temporal rules trust the stated duration.
findings.fix: Floor road durations by distance and region (for example 55 km/h door to door in India beyond 250 km plus breaks), and split or replace drives over about 9 hours with a train or flight.
findings.resolution: trip_validation.implausible_drive_warnings is a first-turn completion gap for drives of 250 km or more averaging over 75 km/h door to door; it asks for a realistic duration or, beyond nine realistic hours, a train, flight or overnight split (3 corpus trips).

findings.title: The existing model judge cannot run on any generated corpus trip
findings.evidence: harness/audit.py passes the whole place cache (3,985 entries, about 13 MB) as places for every generated record, and evals/judge.evidence_for sends it; a judge profile's max_input_bytes is 100 KB. The manifest also stores no request text for any trip and scenario_expectations for only 34.
findings.impact: Milestone 3 judging is unusable on the corpus it was built for, so quality has never been measured at scale.
findings.fix: Send only the plan's own places (evals/trip_text.places_for, added here) and persist request, expectations and producer commit for every generated trip.
findings.resolution: judge.evidence_for sends only the places the plan names, with judge-relevant fields: every corpus judge input is now under 50 KB (median 20 KB, previously about 13 MB). All 178 manifest entries now carry their request (reconstructed and marked request_reconstructed) and expectations; owner_evals reads them from the manifest.

findings.title: The judge's overall score averages hard gates away
findings.evidence: Bali scores 4.00 overall while failing preference fidelity (2/5): it ignored the explicit entry-requirement ask.
findings.impact: Ranking by overall score hides fidelity failures.
findings.fix: Withhold or cap the overall score when a hard gate scores 2 or lower, and report the gate result beside the taste mean.
findings.resolution: judge.validate caps the overall score at a failed hard gate's score (2 or lower) and reports hard_gate_failed; Bali now ranks 2.00 instead of 4.00. Test: tests/test_itinerary_judge.py.

efficiencies.title: Stop attaching the whole 13 MB place cache to every corpus record
efficiencies.evidence: A cProfile of the incremental audit (1,124 s before it was stopped) spent about 95% of its time on JSON encode (386 s), file reads (261 s), JSON decode (176 s) and SHA-256 (66 s) of the place cache, which harness/audit.py passes whole as each generated record's places and harness/incremental.py re-serialises about 13 times per record. The state directory reached 1.6 GB after 113 input snapshots, projecting about 7 GB for one full run. The same payload makes the judge unusable (BL-09). The same audit run through the uncached API path finished in 70 s for 391 records.
efficiencies.plan: Give each record only the places its plan names (evals/trip_text.places_for, widened to the render's lookup keys), or store the cache once by digest and reference it. Expected: a full audit in minutes rather than the projected 30-plus, audit state in MB rather than GB, and a judge request within its 100 KB limit.

efficiencies.title: One stop classifier and a post-lookup identity check before any paid Places call
efficiencies.evidence: places_cache.is_lookupable_place_name (regex) and place_confidence.stop_place_tier (tokens) disagree, and both pass clock times and activity labels. 451 of 3,975 cached resolutions share no word with the stop name; 42 stops resolved to one tour agency, and 17 clock times were paid lookups.
efficiencies.plan: Make place_confidence the single owner, call it from places_cache before lookup, bias each lookup with the day's city rather than the whole destination phrase, and store non-matching results as approximate. It saves Places spend and removes wrong pins in the same change (BL-01).

efficiencies.title: Move plan hygiene from prompt rules and repair turns into a deterministic save-time normaliser
efficiencies.evidence: prompts.py holds about 40 KB of rules, yet 95 of 178 trips list a hotel after the day's departure, 26 are out of time order, 20 keep an unused night, and 75 carry 544 placeholders. Corpus generation measured a median of 5.4 minutes per accepted trip (p90 12.1) at a median ₹38.6, and the August audit's completion-gap gate fired on 236 trips.
efficiencies.plan: Sort and anchor stops, set checkout to the departure date, rebuild day summaries from stops, and count placeholders in code on save. Return only the residual conflicts to the agent (the Lab 19 deterministic-engine direction). The bug class stops occurring instead of being detected, with fewer repair rounds, fewer tokens and less latency.

efficiencies.title: Make the paid corpus self-describing
efficiencies.evidence: 0 of 178 manifest entries store the request text and 34 store scenario expectations; this report had to reconstruct requests from hash-seeded generation matrices. Every generated request phrases an N-day trip across N+1 dates. The 178 trips cost ₹7,469 to produce.
efficiencies.plan: Persist request, expectations, producer commit and model for every generated trip, and fix the date phrase. Fidelity judging and regression comparison can then reuse the corpus indefinitely without paid regeneration.

efficiencies.title: Run the probes on every pull request as a free quality signal
efficiencies.evidence: The eight probes and the place-identity check run over all 178 corpus trips in under 0.5 s with no provider or model call, while the complete suites are suspended from the lane gates.
efficiencies.plan: Promote the probes into the audit rule registry with an accepted baseline, and fail a PR only on a new occurrence on committed corpus trips or golden fixtures, so a behaviour-changing prompt or policy edit is caught before merge.
